A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).

agent.result_text:
All 4 acceptance tests pass on `bin/e2e`.

The whole change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/RollupService.java`:

- **Overdue-total in the figures:** each person's figures, and the sheet's totals, now include an overdue-total. A claim counts as overdue when it is open or pending and its due-by is before the sheet's today. The total adds up those claims' dues, late charge included, and skips any claim whose due is n/a. This is the same rule the screen already uses for `person-overdue-total` and `rollup-overdue-total`, so the audit and the screen agree.
- **When lines are written:** a ROLLUP line is now written when a person's claimed, due-total or overdue-total moved. A TOTALS line is written when any of the three sheet totals moved.
- **New field at the end:** ROLLUP lines end with `overdue-total=<x>` and TOTALS lines end with `overdue-total=<total>`. The existing fields keep their order.
- **Changing today:** this needed no new code. Setting the sheet's today already takes a snapshot before the change and records the rollup after it, so a claim that goes past its due-by, or comes out of overdue, now writes the lines even when no due moved.

I didn't change the front end or the stored data; neither needed it.
